Compare numbers of clusters

Source: R/select_k.R
unsurv_select_k.Rd

Fits unsurv for each candidate K and returns, side by side, the mean silhouette width, the resampling stability of unsurv_stability, the prediction strength of Tibshirani and Walther (2005) and the smallest cluster size.

unsurv_select_k(S, times, K = 2:6, B = 20, splits = 10, seed = NULL, ...)

Arguments

S

Numeric matrix of survival probabilities (\(n \times m\)), columns matching times.

times

Numeric vector of time grid points (length \(m\)).

K

Integer vector of candidate numbers of clusters (each \(\ge 2\)).

B

Integer; number of resamples for the stability index.

splits

Integer; number of random half splits for the prediction strength.

seed

Optional integer seed; NULL uses the current random number stream.

...

Further arguments passed to unsurv (for example distance, weights or eps_jitter).

Value

A data frame with columns K, silhouette, stability, pred_strength and min_size.

Details

The prediction strength of a split into halves \(A\) and \(B\) clusters both halves, assigns the patients of \(B\) to the nearest medoid of the clustering of \(A\) (predict.unsurv), and takes, over the clusters of \(B\), the smallest share of pairs of patients of the same cluster that the medoids of \(A\) also put together. The column reports its mean over splits random splits. Tibshirani and Walther suggest choosing the largest K whose prediction strength exceeds about 0.8. The silhouette and the stability index tend to favour small K, and none of the columns can say that there is no cluster structure; read the table, not only its maxima.

References

Tibshirani, R. and Walther, G. (2005). Cluster validation by prediction strength. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 14(3), 511–528. doi:10.1198/106186005X59243

Examples

if (requireNamespace("cluster", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  times <- seq(0, 4, length.out = 15)
  grp <- sample(1:3, 60, TRUE)
  S <- t(sapply(c(0.15, 0.5, 1.2)[grp] * exp(rnorm(60, 0, 0.1)), function(r) exp(-r * times)))
  unsurv_select_k(S, times, K = 2:4, B = 5, splits = 3, seed = 1)
}
#>   K silhouette stability pred_strength min_size
#> 1 2  0.7561908 0.5935175          1.00       19
#> 2 3  0.8997846 1.0000000          1.00       14
#> 3 4  0.7822307 0.9773106          0.85       13
